William Shakespeare.text: At 18 he married Anne Hathaway, who was 26. His will left her his "second-best bed".
William Shakespeare.evidence: At the age of 18, Shakespeare married 26-year-old Anne Hathaway. ... Some scholars see the bequest as an insult to Anne, whereas others believe that the second-best bed would have been the matrimonial bed and therefore rich in significance.

Agatha Christie.text: She went missing for 11 days in 1926, made headlines worldwide, and never mentioned it in her autobiography.
Agatha Christie.evidence: Following the breakdown of her marriage and the death of her mother in 1926, she made international headlines by going missing for 11 days. ... Christie's autobiography makes no reference to the disappearance.

J. K. Rowling.text: Harry, Ron and Hermione came to her on a train from Manchester to London that was four hours late.
J. K. Rowling.evidence: In mid-1990, she was on a train delayed by four hours from Manchester to London, when the characters Harry Potter, Ron Weasley, and Hermione Granger came plainly into her mind.

Eiichiro Oda.text: One Piece holds the Guinness record for most copies of a comic series by one author: 516 million by 2022.
Eiichiro Oda.evidence: 2022: Guinness World Record for "the most copies published for the same comic book series by a single author" with 516,566,000 copies in printed worldwide up until July 2022.

Barbara Cartland.text: In 1976 she wrote 23 novels, a Guinness record for the most novels written in a single year.
Barbara Cartland.evidence: In addition, in 1976 Cartland wrote 23 novels, earning her the Guinness World Record for the most novels written in a single year.

Danielle Steel.text: By 1999 she had a book on the New York Times bestseller list for 456 weeks in a row, a Guinness record.
Danielle Steel.evidence: In 1999, she was listed in the Guinness Book of World Records for having a book on the New York Times Bestseller List for the most consecutive weeks of any author, 456 at that time.

Georges Simenon.text: Before Maigret he wrote and sold short stories at a rate of 80 typed pages a day.
Georges Simenon.evidence: Simenon was writing and selling short stories at the rate of 80 typed pages a day, and now turned his hand to pulp novels.

Dean Koontz.text: He wrote under ten pen names, one of them inspired by his golden retriever, Trixie.
Dean Koontz.evidence: Koontz has stated on his website that he used only the ten known pen names ... One of Koontz's pen names was inspired by his dog, Trixie Koontz, a Golden Retriever, shown in many of his book-jacket photos.

Leo Tolstoy.text: He was nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature every year from 1902 to 1906 and never won.
Leo Tolstoy.evidence: He received nominations for the Nobel Prize in Literature every year from 1902 to 1906 and for the Nobel Peace Prize in 1901, 1902, and 1909. ... Tolstoy never being awarded a Nobel Prize remains a major Nobel Prize controversy.

Enid Blyton.text: The BBC once kept her books off the air for being "second-rate" and without merit.
Enid Blyton.evidence: Did you know: ... that Enid Blyton's books were banned by the BBC for being "second-rate" and without merit?
